title_jp: ひらがなさえ{読めなかった|よめなかった}
context: Friday 18 December, a quiet afternoon at ゲストハウス{風|かぜ}: {健太|けんた} asks アルちゃん how he started learning Japanese. He tells him about his language exchange with {由紀|ゆき} in Spain, and about being called ずくなし by {恵子|けいこ}さん the night before.
scene: Friday, a quiet hour at reception. {健太|けんた} wants to know how you learned Japanese. You tell him, and confess last night's mystery word.

phrases.jp: {日本|にほん}に{来る|くる}{前|まえ}は、{箸|はし|chopsticks|3}さえ{使えなかった|つかえなかった}。
phrases.en: Before I came to Japan, I couldn't even use chopsticks.
phrases.note: Noun + さえ + negative = not even.

phrases.jp: {何|なん}のこっちゃ{分からへん|わからへん|(Kansai) = 分からない|2}。
phrases.en: No idea what that's supposed to mean.
phrases.note: Kansai for {何|なん}のことか{分|わ}からない. {健太|けんた}'s reaction to anything strange.

phrases.jp: {聞き間違えた|ききまちがえた|to mishear|3}みたい。
phrases.note: {聞|き}く hear + {間違|まちが}える get wrong. Saves face in any misunderstanding.

phrases.jp: {言語|げんご|language|3}{交換|こうかん|exchange|3}の{相手|あいて|partner|3}を{探して|さがして}います。
phrases.en: I'm looking for a language exchange partner.
phrases.note: What you'd write on a poster or an app profile.

phrases.jp: {毎日|まいにち}{続ける|つづける|to keep doing|4}のが{大事|だいじ}だよ。
phrases.en: The important thing is to keep at it every day.
phrases.note: Verb + のが{大事|だいじ} = what matters is …ing.

dialogue_setting: Reception at ゲストハウス{風|かぜ}, Friday afternoon. No check-ins until four.

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: アルちゃんの{日本語|にほんご}、{最初|さいしょ}はどうやって{勉強|べんきょう}したん？
dialogue.en: Your Japanese, アルちゃん: how did you start learning it?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: スペインで{由紀|ゆき}と{言語|げんご|language|3}{交換|こうかん|exchange|3}を{始めた|はじめた}のが{きっかけ||how it started, trigger|3}。{最初|さいしょ}はひらがなさえ{読めなかった|よめなかった}よ。
dialogue.en: It started with a language exchange with {由紀|ゆき} in Spain. At first I couldn't even read hiragana.

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: ほんまに？{今|いま}はめっちゃ{喋れる|しゃべれる|to chat, talk|4}やん。{俺|おれ}なんか、{英語|えいご}は{挨拶|あいさつ|greeting|4}さえ{怪しい|あやしい|shaky, doubtful|3}で。
dialogue.en: Seriously? You can really talk now. Me, my English is shaky even for 'hello'.
dialogue.note: ほんまに = {本当|ほんとう}に; やん = じゃない; で = よ (Kansai).

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: でも{昨日|きのう}の{夜|よる}、{恵子|けいこ}さんに「ずくなし」って{言われて|いわれて}…{意味|いみ}さえ{分からなかった|わからなかった}。
dialogue.en: But last night {恵子|けいこ}さん called me 'zukunashi'… I didn't even know what it meant.

dialogue.speaker: 健太
dialogue.jp: ははっ、{怠け者|なまけもの|lazy person|2}って{意味|いみ}や。{関西|かんさい}{人|じん}の{俺|おれ}も、{最初|さいしょ}は{何|なん}のこっちゃ{思った|おもった}わ。
dialogue.en: Ha! It means 'lazy bones'. Being from Kansai, I had no clue either at first.
dialogue.note: や = だ; 何のこっちゃ = 何のことだ (Kansai).

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: やっぱり…。こたつから{出られなくて|でられなくて}、{雪かき|ゆきかき|snow shovelling|3}さえ{手伝わなかった|てつだわなかった}から。
dialogue.en: I knew it… I couldn't get out of the kotatsu and didn't even help shovel the snow.

listening.intro: {健太|けんた} gives you his one piece of language advice.

lines.jp: {毎日|まいにち}ちょっとずつでも{続ける|つづける|to keep doing|4}のが、{一番|いちばん}やで。
lines.en: Keeping at it every day, even a little, is what counts most.

grammar.form: noun + さえ (ひらがなさえ, {挨拶|あいさつ}さえ) · noun + で / に + さえ ({子|こ}どもでさえ, {私|わたし}にさえ) · verb ます-stem + さえ + しない ({見|み}さえしない)
grammar.explanation: さえ picks the most basic, obvious case and says even that is true (usually 'not even'). It's stronger and a bit more written than も: ひらがなさえ{読|よ}めない sounds more shocking than ひらがなも. Don't confuse it with さえ〜ば, 'as long as'.

examples.jp: この{漢字|かんじ}は、{日本人|にほんじん}の{子|こ}どもでさえ{読める|よめる}。
examples.en: Even Japanese kids can read this kanji.

examples.jp: {忙しくて|いそがしくて}、{名前|なまえ}さえ{聞けなかった|きけなかった}。
examples.en: It was so busy I didn't even get to ask her name.

examples.jp: {颯太|そうた}は{宿題|しゅくだい}を{見|み}さえしない。
examples.en: {颯太|そうた} won't even look at his homework.

quiz.question: {疲れて|つかれて}、ご{飯|はん}＿＿{食べられなかった|たべられなかった}。
quiz.en: I was so tired I couldn't even eat.
quiz.explain: さえ + negative = not even the most basic thing.

quiz_more.question: {専門家|せんもんか|expert|3}＿＿{分からない|わからない}{問題|もんだい}だ。
quiz_more.en: It's a problem even experts don't understand.
quiz_more.explain: With a person as subject, use でさえ: even experts.

quiz_more.question: {彼|かれ}は{私|わたし}の{顔|かお}を{見|み}＿＿しなかった。
quiz_more.en: He didn't even look at my face.
quiz_more.explain: ます-stem + さえしない = won't even do it.

kanji.where: On the {翻訳|ほんやく}アプリ {健太|けんた} opens on the reception tablet to check 'zukunashi'. It finds nothing.
kanji.breakdown: {翻|ほん} flip over + {訳|やく} translate, meaning → flipping words over into another language.
kanji.related: {通訳|つうやく} = interpreting (spoken), {翻訳|ほんやく} = translating (written).

tip.title: ずく: Nagano's favourite word
tip.body: In Nagano, ずく is the energy to get things done. ずくがある = hard-working, ずくなし = lazy, ずくを{出|だ}す = make the effort. Outside Nagano almost nobody knows it, so it's a fun word to drop when you visit elsewhere.

challenge.prompt: That evening {健太|けんた} on LINE: 「{明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}、{一緒|いっしょ}に{雪かき|ゆきかき}やろか。ずくなし{卒業|そつぎょう}や！」 Tell him: got it, you're in!
challenge.explanation: {健太|けんた} invites you to shovel snow with him, and you agree, so {了解|りょうかい}！ fits. {眠|ねむ}い… or ガーン would sound like you'd rather stay in the kotatsu, and うーん… is hesitating: exactly what a ずくなし would send.

vocab.note: Formal word; in chat people say {言葉|ことば}. {言語交換|げんごこうかん} = language exchange.
{交換|こうかん}する. Also for swapping LINE: LINE{交換|こうかん}.
〜のがきっかけ = it all started with …
Casual {話|はな}す. Also means chatty: よく{喋|しゃべ}る{人|ひと}.
Also a short speech: {挨拶|あいさつ}をお{願|ねが}いします.
Suspicious person or shaky skills: {英語|えいご}が{怪|あや}しい.
{怠|なま}ける be lazy + {者|もの} person. Also the sloth!
{言|い}い{間違|まちが}える = to misspeak.
{話|はな}し{相手|あいて} = someone to talk to.
Verb stem + {続|つづ}ける: {読|よ}み{続|つづ}ける = keep reading.

kanji_study.parts: 扌 hand radical + 奐 (a person holding something out) → hands passing things back and forth: exchange.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 喚 (call out): 喚 has 口 mouth on the left, 換 has 扌 hand.

kanji_study.parts: 門 gate + 关 a bar across it → the bar that locks a gate: a checkpoint. Things that pass through it are 'connected'.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 開 (open): 開 has 开 inside the gate, 関 has 关 with two dots on top.

extras.title: More Nagano words
extras.intro: Ones you might hear from {田中|たなか}さん's generation.

items.en: to make the effort, get going
items.note: ずくを{出|だ}せ！ = come on, get moving!

extras.title: How it started
extras.title_jp: {始まり|はじまり}を{話す|はなす}
extras.intro: Ways to tell how something began.

items.jp: {友達|ともだち}に{誘われた|さそわれた}のがきっかけです。
items.en: It started when a friend invited me.

items.jp: アニメを{見て|みて}、{興味|きょうみ|interest|4}を{持った|もった}んです。
items.en: I got interested after watching anime.

items.jp: {気がついたら|きがついたら|before I knew it|4}、{夢中|むちゅう}になっていた。
items.en: Before I knew it, I was hooked.
